# Incident Report — MTA 2026-02-28 Packet Capture Analysis

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (15,512 frames, SHA256 `3dc470f5490ec15b4024c513e87c67e0b17caeae2a2ce3d83541be24ef407e61`)
- Capture window: 2026-02-28 23:55:06 → 2026-03-01 04:16:35 (~4h 21m)
- No separate IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived entirely from packet-level analysis with tshark.

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.2.28.88 |
| MAC address | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR |
| AD domain | EASYAS123.TECH (domain controller: EASYAS123-DC, 10.2.28.2) |
| Logged-in Windows user | brolf (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `brolf`, realm EASYAS123.TECH) |

DHCP confirms the host is a Windows client (option 12 hostname DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR, requested lease 10.2.28.88 from server 10.2.28.1). NBNS registrations for `DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR` and workgroup/site name `EASYAS123` corroborate.

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious abuse of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client/gateway protocol).

**Attribution basis: signature-confirmed.** The traffic exhibits the exact, distinctive NetSupport Manager client-gateway wire protocol, not merely behavioral heuristics:
- Fixed request URI `POST /fakeurl.htm`
- `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`
- `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)`
- Protocol body fields `CMD=POLL`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1` on check-in, and `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>` on tasking/response exchanges

This exact combination of URI, User-Agent, Server banner, and CMD field set is unique to NetSupport Manager's client/gateway handshake and is the standard signature used to identify NetSupport RAT in commodity malware distribution campaigns (frequently delivered via fake browser-update lures). No dropper/PE download appears inside this capture window, so the initial infection vector predates the capture; the host was already beaconing within 45 seconds of the capture start.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- C2 IP:port — `45.131.214.85:443` (traffic is plaintext HTTP over the port, not TLS — a NetSupport Gateway camouflage technique)
- C2 domain — `vadusa.xyz` (resolved by victim DNS query at t=44.77s to `45.131.214.85`)
- C2 URL — `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm`

**Beaconing pattern**
- 264 POST requests to `45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` observed from first check-in at 23:55:51 UTC+4 (t=45.05s) through the end of the capture at 04:16:28 UTC+4 (t=15682s), roughly every 60 seconds — persistent, capture-duration C2 beaconing.

**Transferred files / hashes**
- No executable/PE payload transfer was observed inside this capture (no `MZ`-header HTTP objects, no octet-stream/exe content-types delivered to the victim). Consequently no file name or SHA256 can be grounded in this evidence for the malware binary itself; the payload was already resident on the host prior to capture start.
- All other exported HTTP objects in the capture (Windows Update/BITS `.cab`/filestreamingservice downloads, OCSP responses, `connecttest.txt`) are legitimate Microsoft/Adobe housekeeping traffic and are not part of this incident.

**Traffic explicitly ruled out as noise (reviewed and eliminated)**
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` (resolves to legitimate Akamai IPs 23.218.232.161/.148) — genuine Adobe Acrobat update-check traffic, not malicious.
- `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `ocsp.digicert.com`, Microsoft telemetry/BITS domains — standard Windows/Office background traffic.

## Summary
Host **DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88 / 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad)**, logged on as domain user **brolf** in the **EASYAS123.TECH** AD environment, is actively infected with **NetSupport RAT**. It has been beaconing to **vadusa.xyz (45.131.214.85:443)** roughly every 60 seconds for the entire capture window using the fixed NetSupport client-gateway protocol (`POST /fakeurl.htm`, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`). Recommend immediate isolation of 10.2.28.88, credential reset for user `brolf`, and blocking of `45.131.214.85` and `vadusa.xyz` at the perimeter. The initial infection vector is not captured in this evidence and requires endpoint/EDR artifacts to determine.
